name: Nucleus accumbens
summary: The ventral striatum, where the head of the caudate and the putamen merge beneath the anterior limb of the internal capsule, next to the septal area. It receives dopamine from the ventral tegmental area (mesolimbic pathway) and input from the amygdala, hippocampus and prefrontal cortex, and projects to the ventral pallidum. It encodes reward prediction and motivation, is the substrate of addiction and of apathy, and is a target of deep brain stimulation for obsessive-compulsive disorder and depression.

anatomy.location: Ventromedial striatum at the junction of the caudate head and putamen beneath the anterior limb of the internal capsule, lateral to the septal nuclei and above the olfactory tubercle, at the level of the anterior commissure.

subdivisions.name: Core
subdivisions.note: motor aspects of motivated behavior; projects to the ventral pallidum

subdivisions.name: Shell
subdivisions.note: limbic, connected with the hypothalamus and extended amygdala; drug reward

function: Reward processing, motivation and incentive salience, reinforcement learning, integration of limbic drive into action.

bestView.label: ventral striatum below the anterior limb of the internal capsule
junction of caudate head and putamen at the level of the anterior commissure

imaging.normalAppearance: Gray matter bridging the caudate and putamen ventrally on coronal T1 at the level of the anterior commissure; the MASSP mesh in this atlas outlines it. Rarely abnormal on routine imaging.

pathology.finding: Restriction of the caudate head and ventral striatum; abulia and apathy.
Electrode in the ventral striatum/anterior limb.

lesionEffects.deficit: Addiction and compulsive behaviors (dysfunction rather than lesion)
Improvement of obsessive-compulsive symptoms with stimulation

examination: Motivation and interest on history from patient and family
Screen for substance use and compulsive behaviors
pearls: Apathy after a caudate or ventral striatal stroke is a lesion, not depression; it responds poorly to antidepressants and better to dopaminergic drugs
Dopamine agonists can produce compulsive gambling through this circuit
